Class SinglesColumn

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somestacks.block.StackRun<SinglesStackBE>
com.github.crittscott.somestacks.block.SinglesColumn
All Implemented Interfaces:
StackRunItemAccess
public final class SinglesColumn extends StackRun<SinglesStackBE>
A maximal contiguous vertical run of Singles Stacks, addressed as one inventory by automation.

Cells are a structure, not a bag: a slot index is a position and every item must rest on the cell beneath it or on the seam with the Singles Stack below. So insertion places one item at the cell it is given, and only where that cell is empty and supported, growing the column when the cell lies in the block above it. Refusing an unsupported cell rather than choosing another is what keeps a slot index meaning one place, and no placement can leave an item hanging in the air.

Automation uses the same extraction behavior as the player: the target cell is emptied and its visual column shifts down without drops or horizontal movement. Singles cannot use the Bar column's topmost-item backfill because different items are not interchangeable.

An instance describes the run bounds at resolution time. Block entities cache it for the current tick, and placement or removal invalidates every affected cache immediately.

    • insertAt

      public int insertAt(int flatSlot, net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack stack, boolean simulate)
      Places one item at flatSlot, growing the column when that cell lies in the block above it.

      Answering for the cell it was given rather than for the column is what makes the handler's slot range mean something: a caller that walks the range and sums what each cell accepts gets the column's real capacity; reporting whole-column capacity at every cell would multiply it.

      A caller walking the range in ascending order still fills the column, because each placement stands before the next cell is offered: a filled layer supports the layer above it by the time the walk arrives there.

      Parameters:
      simulate - when true, nothing is placed
      Returns:
      how many items were, or would be, taken from stack

    • acceptsAt

      public int acceptsAt(int flatSlot, net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack stack, IntFunction<net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack> contents)
      One item if flatSlot is an empty cell whose supporting cell is occupied, reading cells through contents; otherwise none. A bottom-layer cell rests on the same visual column of the block below, whose rotation may differ, and the bottom block of all rests on the world.

      A cell in the block above the column is checked against the block growth would put there — unrotated as a player's own placement is, standing on the column's top layer — and against the side-effect-free checks in canGrow(VoxelShape). A simulation therefore cannot promise a cell the commit would refuse.

    • extract

      public net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack extract(int flatSlot, int amount, boolean simulate)
      Takes the item at flatSlot through the block's own removal, so automation and the player leave the column in the same state: the cells above the hole shift down one layer in that column, drawing from the Singles Stacks above and removing any block the walk empties.
      Parameters:
      flatSlot - the position to extract, numbered from the bottom block upward
      amount - the requested maximum; any positive value can extract the position's one item
      simulate - whether to report the result without changing the column
      Returns:
      the one item at flatSlot, or an empty stack when extraction is not possible
